title: No blame in case of fatal cocaine overdose during RCMP traffic stop
article: An inquest has found the RCMP blameless in the death of a Manitoba man who died convulsing next to a police cruiser after he had gulped a condom full of cocaine.
Associate Chief Judge Michel Chartier says in his inquest report that Mounties and paramedics could have done nothing differently to save Randy George Krasnesky.
The 35-year-old man died in the Selkirk hospital in March 2007, about one hour after he and a female friend were stopped by police in connection with possible drug dealing.
The inquest heard Krasnesky's behaviour quickly changed when he was placed in a cruiser and that his friend told police she had no idea what he may have swallowed.
An autopsy turned up cocaine in Krasnesky's body 10 times the amount that's killed other people.
An RCMP officer told the inquest there is no specific training on drug-swallowing, and no mandatory review of RCMP policies contained in their operations manual.
